source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check ME firmware operation status is normal.
1. Check the information of test item

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Information should be correct and still be correct after rebooting

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ls /sys/class/mei/ 2>&1; echo ---; mei-amt-check -S 2>&1 || echo "ME Firmware Operation Status tool not installed"; echo ---; dmesg | grep -iE "operation|status" | tail -20
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: read the ME operation status (ME Firmware Operation Status) via the MEI/SPS channel. The agent collects whatever MEI/SPS registers/dmesg lines are reachable; confirming the value is CORRECT requires knowing the expected value (a user-supplied baseline), so this is PARTIAL: agent returns the raw readout, user judges it against the expected ME Firmware Operation Status.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: read-only attempt against Intel MEI/SPS registers using vendor tools (intelmetool / mei-amt-check) that may not be installed on the SUT; install/availability must be confirmed first, and the expected baseline value must be provided by the user.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; identifies a raw MEI operation-state read but does not validate mei-amt-check -S semantics, define normal operation or implement reboot persistence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; requires expected operation state, platform/tool identity, read-only behavior and controlled pre/post reboot collection.
historical_reviews.round_02: PARTIAL; returns an owner-judged readout but does not separate capability, readiness and verdict.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: Confirms the missing normal-state definition and safe-query/reboot evidence requirements.

original_test_intent: Read the Intel ME firmware operational-state field for the identified platform, compare it with the owner-defined normal operating state and verify that it remains normal after an approved reboot.
original_method: Run a documented read-only MEI operation-status query, retain raw output and decoded operational state, execute one approved controlled reboot, repeat the same query and compare both results with the platform-specific normal-state definition.
manual_activity: The authorized user defines normal operation, validates the diagnostic and reboot plan and later issues the verdict. The query, reboot, reconnect, repeated query and comparison are entirely electronic and can be automated.
required_inputs: Exact platform/SKU and ME/SPS firmware/operation-state identity
Authoritative expected operation-status field/code and decode
Approved read-only MEI utility/version/exact syntax and target selection
Maintenance approval, active-workload check, reconnect timeout and OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Do not invoke ME operational transitions, provisioning, resets, writes or firmware changes.
Do not infer the operation state from generic dmesg 'operation|status' lines.
Preserve existing logs and obtain explicit approval before the service-impacting reboot.
Stop on ambiguous target/output, unexpected operation state, diagnostic side effect or recovery anomaly; never auto-retry.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the operation-state definition and read-only query; inventory platform/ME identity and capture raw/decoded pre-reboot state.
Perform one approved reboot and monitor controlled downtime and reconnect.
Repeat the identical query, compare expected/pre/post operation state and collect kernel/BMC/SEL health without setting PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Provide the platform-specific normal ME operation status and approve the diagnostic utility.
Approve reboot, maintenance and recovery limits.
Review the raw/decoded evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: sysfs is useful for MEI presence, but generic dmesg matches cannot prove ME operation status. mei-amt-check -S target and read-only semantics require validation, and the command omits the post-reboot query.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the vendor/project-approved read-only ME operation-status query for this platform, capturing the same field before and after one approved reboot.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: ME Firmware Operation Status normality, post-reboot correctness and 5/0-minute fields are preserved without inventing a status code.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture a structured operation-status field with raw code, vendor decode and exact ME identity using identical pre/post reboot queries and the supplied normal-state definition.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the ME/SPS generation and mode covered by the supplied utility documentation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record ME/SPS firmware, BIOS, MEI driver, diagnostic utility, OS and kernel.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Use platform/vendor ME operation-status and diagnostic documentation supplied for the project.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines the operational-state field and closes the missing reboot/re-query step.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; normal operation before and after reboot is required.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Normal operation-state code/decode and validated query.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Operational status can be transient during boot; sampling phase and post-reconnect stabilization must be defined.

project_override_considerations: A project defines the normal operational state, stabilization interval and reboot plan. These inputs and engineer judgment do not reduce automation capability; report the exact sampling phase and platform.
expected_evidence: Platform/SKU, BIOS/ME/SPS/MEI identity and query-tool manifest
Normal operation-status field/code/decode and sampling rule
Raw/decoded pre-reboot status, approved reboot/downtime/reconnect transcript and raw/decoded stabilized post-reboot status
Comparison, kernel/BMC/SEL health, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently asks for normal ME operation status and persistence after reboot. Missing field definition and sampling/query details are readiness inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operational-state persistence intent is clear. Missing project parameters and packages are not permanent BLOCKED, and no manual core action is inherently required.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains its package/baseline warning but rejects generic evidence and the PARTIAL capability label.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its safe-tool, platform and reboot controls while reclassifying to FULLY AUTOMATABLE under the V3.1 readiness/capability separation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Adds sampling-phase control and distinguishes operational state from general firmware status and raw status-value sibling cases.

review_improvement: Avoids false status inference from logs, makes transient boot-state sampling reproducible and preserves full automation despite owner inputs and verdict ownership.
independent_technical_reasoning: The ME operational state can be queried and compared programmatically before and after a controlled reboot. User approval and a supplied expected state affect readiness, not the automatable nature of the core sequence.
